constitutive_assumptions: The thumb interphalangeal (IP) and metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints are assumed to act as simple planar hinge joints.
The thumb carpometacarpal (CMC) joint is assumed to behave as a special spherical hinge joint constrained within the thumb motion space, with twisting motion coupled to abduction/adduction.
Thumb skeletal segments are assumed to be rigid vectors connecting anatomical joint rotation centers.
Tendon cables (fishing lines) are assumed to transmit tension along designated routing paths without elongation or bidirectional driving capability without antagonistic pairs or pulley mechanisms.
Contact surfaces on the glove are designed with soft material for patient safety, whereas palm/dorsal supports and pipelines are rigid to sustain mechanical loads.
control_variables: Actuator travel distance limit (50 mm) and motor peak force rating (50 N).
Allowable maximum interaction force threshold set via GUI software to avoid excessive tissue loading.
Rest interval between sequential pressing/releasing actions during force characterization (7 seconds).
Trajectory angle-to-position mapping derived from pre-recorded healthy subject experimental motion profile.
Fixed optical marker placement sites on anatomical bony landmarks across evaluation trials.
dependent_variables: Thumb fingertip force generation (peak force, continuous force capability, baseline release force).
Thumb 3D fingertip and joint motion trajectories.
Thumb joint angles across time: CMC(z), CMC(x), MCP, and IP.
Range of motion (ROM) across individual joints and average ROM across all thumb joints.
Fingertip trajectory curve arc length (ARC LENGTH).
Similarity index (SI) of ROM and ARC LENGTH compared to a healthy subject reference.
Completion status of functional activities of daily living and rehabilitation tasks.

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A hybrid actuation architecture integrating a tendon-driven flexible link with direct fingertip tendons enables multi-DoF thumb movements (abduction/adduction and flexion/extension) while mitigating tendon attachment point shifting.
Integrating a series elastic actuation (SEA) mechanism with pulleys allows bidirectional actuation and simultaneous release of opposing tendons, driving full-hand DoFs with four linear actuators.

Thumb kinematics can be modeled by treating the CMC joint as a constrained non-orthogonal spherical joint, tracking joint coordinate axes, and estimating orientation through Rodrigues' rotation formula under wrist displacement.

Tendon-driven exoskeleton assistance doubled thumb fingertip force from ~5 N to over 10 N, enabled sustained rather than impulsive force, and eliminated a 2 N residual resting force to allow full release.

Exoskeleton assistance enlarged the stroke patient's thumb encircling area from 0.53 cm^2 to 48.7 cm^2 (healthy reference: 128.9 cm^2) and bottle grasping arc length from 0.67 cm to 5.46 cm (healthy reference: 7.85 cm).

Post-stroke joint alterations such as spasticity and elevated joint stiffness, combined with underactuated robot constraints, create inevitable trajectory deviations between assisted patient motion and healthy benchmarks.

experimental_setup: Wearable glove fabricated using multimaterial 3D printing (Stratasys J735) with rigid load-bearing supports/tubing and soft skin-interface elements, secured with a soft wristband.
Backpack-mounted remote actuation system (RAS) housing four micro servo linear motors (INSPIRE-ROBOTS LAF50), motor driver board (AES-LA-31-06), and a lithium battery.
Computer control interface running on a touchscreen for task selection, trajectory generation, and safety emergency halting.
Fingertip force measurement apparatus utilizing a load cell pressure sensor (FUTEK LSB200) to evaluate pressing and releasing profiles.
Motion tracking system utilizing an optical capture system (OptiTrack, LEYARO) and reflective markers attached to the wrist, CMC, MCP, IP joints, and thumb tip.
Human participant testing conducted under rehabilitation medical supervision, evaluating one 46-year-old stroke patient with hemiplegia alongside one 26-year-old healthy subject.
future_work: Investigating approaches to minimize kinematic trajectory mismatch between patient motion and healthy references.
Combining the hand exoskeleton with a soft upper-limb exoskeleton to provide coordinated assistance across both hand and arm motions.
Implementing biological signal-based active intention control, including EEG and EMG interfaces, for self-directed rehabilitation tasks.
independent_variables: Assistance mode: voluntary unassisted motion (Stroke-vol, Health-vol) versus exoskeleton-assisted motion (Stroke-exo).
Subject neurological status: healthy participant versus hemiplegic stroke patient.
Task type: thumb fingertip force pressing/releasing, thumb encircling, bottle grasping, and six functional rehabilitation/ADL tasks.
limitations_inferred: The experimental evaluation was conducted on a single stroke patient and a single healthy control, limiting statistical generalization across different hand sizes and impairment levels.
Optical motion tracking is subject to marker occlusion during certain functional hand gestures, such as turning over a piece of paper.
Trajectory planning relied on pre-calibrated look-up tables from a healthy subject rather than adaptive, real-time closed-loop user-interaction modeling.
Long-term motor recovery and neuroplasticity benefits were not assessed longitudinally beyond immediate task-execution trials.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Kinematic mismatches exist between assisted patient trajectories and target profiles due to post-stroke joint stiffness/spasticity and underactuated hand exoskeleton architecture.
The device does not assist arm movements, obliging the stroke patient to physically support the paretic limb with their unimpaired arm during reach-dependent tasks.
The control architecture is currently limited to a manual touch-screen GUI without active biological signal control (such as EEG or EMG).
Donning and doffing requires approximately 2 minutes with external assistance from another person.
main_results: Fingertip force capability improved from ~5 N (voluntary) to >10 N (with exoskeleton), transformed impulsive pressing into sustained force, and reduced resting baseline force from ~2 N to 0 N to enable complete release.
Thumb encircling workspace area (AREA) increased from 0.53 cm^2 unassisted to 48.7 cm^2 assisted, with average joint ROM similarity index rising from 20% to 80%.
Bottle grasping thumb trajectory arc length (ARC LENGTH) expanded from 0.67 cm unassisted to 5.46 cm assisted, with average joint ROM similarity index increasing from 12% to 60%.

The stroke patient successfully executed all six functional ADL training tasks (block throwing, card pinching, key inserting, pin moving, paper turning, letter writing) with assistance, while achieving none unassisted.
The lightweight glove (<200 g) achieved dexterous multi-DoF thumb and full-digit actuation utilizing only four actuators through the hybrid tendon and flexible-link architecture.
modeling_methods: Planar kinematic modeling for thumb MCP and IP hinge joints.
Constrained spherical hinge joint kinematic modeling for the thumb CMC joint with non-orthogonal CMC(x) and CMC(z) angular definitions.
Rodrigues' rotation formula combined with translation vectors to track coordinate frame shifts caused by wrist translation and rotation.
Surface fitting in MATLAB (z = f(x, y)) to integrate surface AREA for thumb encircling trajectories.
Curve fitting in MATLAB to integrate ARC LENGTH for thumb fingertip movement profiles.
performance_metrics: Fingertip motion trajectory arc length (ARC LENGTH, cm).
Joint range of motion (ROM, degrees) for CMC(z), CMC(x), MCP, IP, and overall thumb average.
Similarity Index (SI, %) of ROM and ARC LENGTH relative to healthy benchmark movements.
Donning and doffing duration (~2 minutes with assistance).
Functional task completion success rate across six ADL paradigms.
possible_gap_implications: Integrating tunable or variable stiffness elements into soft wearable exoskeletons could allow the device to match patient joint resistance and adapt to stroke-induced spasticity.
Developing multi-segment continuum mechanic models for hybrid tendon-flexible link systems could enhance trajectory tracking fidelity across non-orthogonal anatomical joints.
Co-designing distal soft hand exoskeletons with proximal soft continuum arm manipulators could resolve the limitation of unassisted arm transport in post-stroke motor therapy.
paper.research_objective: To design, model, and experimentally validate a lightweight tendon-driven soft hand exoskeleton employing a hybrid flexible-link and tendon mechanism that achieves multi-degree-of-freedom thumb movements and full-hand actuation using a minimal number of actuators (four in total) for post-stroke grasping assistance and rehabilitation.
paper.research_problem: Accommodating sufficient actuators within the compact, narrow digit space (especially the thumb) to realize high-DoF assistance in hand exoskeletons without adding excessive weight, causing joint misalignment, shifting tendon attachment points, or severely restricting thumb range of motion.
paper.title: Soft Exoskeleton With Fully Actuated Thumb Movements for Grasping Assistance
